methods: Read current AGENTS.md first and applied parent-provided latest user audit/test gate; no prior audit verdict or historical/adjacent archive source used.
Frozen-snapshot names provided exact scope. Each inspected file has its current byte SHA-256, separately checked at report time; whole-repository ending digest uses unmodified scripts/snapshot.mjs.

Focused manual cross-file review covered installation, HTTPS activation and recovery, DNS recipes/credentials, archive validation/build staging, upgrades, administrator reset, provider registry/layers/model catalogs, native identity/launcher and actual project creation.
AST structural inspection is reported separately from full-text review; test method/call coverage is not represented as executing tests or reading every assertion predicate.
Narrow offline monkeypatched fsync tracing exercised the actual create_project_from_input implementation in a fresh task-owned temporary native home.
Offline Caddy source pin/Go lock structure check read current repository material only; no dependency fetch or build occurred.

findings.title: Persist the newly created projects directory before reporting project creation success
findings.trigger: First successful project creation when native_home/projects does not yet exist; also a retry following interruption after creating that root.
findings.description: root.mkdir publishes native_home/projects, then project.mkdir publishes the child. Only fsync_directory(root) runs before the helper returns success. This synchronizes entries within projects but does not establish persistence of the projects name in native_home. The higher-level project registration can be durably committed after success while an abrupt reboot can lose that newly published ancestor entry.
findings.impact: A successfully registered first project can point to a missing directory after abrupt host failure; this violates durable publication before success. Ordinary non-crash creation succeeds.
reproduce: Run the ignored offline probe with the supplied Python: .work/audit2_deploy_project_probe.py.
The probe uses a fresh temporary native home and patches fsync_directory only to record its arguments.
Observe a successful result while fsyncCallsRelativeToNativeHome equals ["projects"] and nativeHomeSynced equals false.
findings.expected: After root.mkdir and its directory/symlink checks, synchronize native_home before creating/publishing the project; do this even when projects already exists to cover interrupted retries. Also review synchronization of the newly created empty project directory itself before returning success.
findings.validationBoundary: Confirmed actual helper call ordering only. No power cut, destructive reboot, service changes or Linux filesystem durability experiment was performed.
findings.testGap: Both project-creation unit tests and native-identity project tests exercise ordinary success/error/ownership paths but do not require ancestor-directory durability.

limitations: Complete means every scoped source file was inspected using the explicitly recorded method, not that every file had full-text review or that all runtime behavior was exercised.

Twelve production helpers and most tests received AST structural inspection; this method has less semantic detail than a full line-by-line read, and bounded extracted expressions may truncate long guards.
go.mod/go.sum review verifies pinned material consistency and lock structure, not correctness/security of all external dependency source.
Production Linux behaviors and external services remain unexecuted in this round.
The single durability finding establishes a missing persistence barrier, not measured data loss under a physical power interruption.
